title: Bank Transfer Timing
summary: Says when an Indian bank transfer will actually arrive on IMPS, NEFT, RTGS or UPI, and catches amounts the chosen rail will refuse.
description: Reads back when money arrives on the chosen rail (IMPS/UPI instantly, the next half-hourly NEFT batch plus up to 2 hours, RTGS within 30 minutes) and catches RTGS under ₹2 lakh, IMPS over ₹5 lakh, UPI over its category cap, bank limits and new-payee caps.
catches: RTGS below the ₹2 lakh minimum and IMPS above ₹5 lakh per transaction
UPI amounts above the per-transaction or 24-hour cap for the category
Your bank's own daily limit, and a new payee's cooling period or first-day cap
Late arrival: the next NEFT batch, the last batch landing at 00:00, branch hours and holidays
Offers the rail that would work, and spells the amount in lakh and crore
limits: Rail limits are built in as of the verification date; banks may set lower caps, and NPCI/RBI can change them
Bank limits, new-payee rules and holidays come only from the props you pass
Arrival times are the regulator's expected timelines, not a guarantee for a specific transfer
a11y: Rails are a role="radiogroup" of role="radio" buttons with roving tabIndex and arrow-key navigation
The continue button uses aria-disabled rather than disabled while blocked
Status is announced in a role="status" region
Issues use text and icons, not colour alone
server: The bank or payment provider enforces the real limits; validate the amount, rail and payee on the server and use idempotency for the transfer.

rules.note: Informational; check the official source. NEFT (half-hourly batches, credit within 2 hours), RTGS (₹2 lakh minimum, credit within 30 minutes) and IMPS (₹5 lakh) were checked against RBI/NPCI pages. The UPI category caps were not re-checked: the NPCI circular is a scanned PDF with no readable text.

stops: Transfer refused or credited a day late
